extracted.intended_audience: general partners, sponsors, issuer counsel and preparers of prospectuses/registration statements for roll-up transactions under SEC Regulation S-K
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and disclosure items for a principal disclosure document/prospectus describing a roll-up transaction involving partnerships, including required summaries, risk disclosures, comparative information, valuations, fairness opinions, and pro forma financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 903 — Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide in the forepart of the disclosure document a clear, concise and comprehensible summary of the roll-up transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary shall include a summary description of each of the following items and any other material terms or consequences necessary to an understanding of the transaction: (1) each material risk and effect on investors (including changes in business plan, voting rights, cash distribution policies, form of ownership interest or management compensation; general partner conflicts of interest; likelihood securities received will trade below assigned value); (2) material terms of the roll-up transaction, including the valuation method used to allocate securities in the successor; (3) whether the general partner reasonably believes the transaction is fair or unfair to investors, with bases; (4) any outside party opinion concerning fairness, whether it addresses all combinations of partnerships, and contacts with outside parties concerning fairness opinions, valuations or reports (see Item 911(a)(5)); (5) the background of and reasons for the roll-up and alternatives (see Item 908(b)); (6) rights of investors to dissenters' or appraisal rights or similar rights and to obtain a list of investors; and (7) if affiliates may participate or receive compensation, an organizational chart showing relationships between general partner, sponsor and affiliates. Instruction: the description of the material risks and effects required must be presented prominently in the forepart of the summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 904 — Risk factors and other considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately following the summary, describe in reasonable detail each material risk and effect of the roll-up transaction on investors in each partnership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: (1) potential risks, adverse effects and benefits for investors and the general partner, including those from matters described in Item 905 (with cross references); (2) material risks arising from an investment in the successor; (3) the likelihood that successor securities will trade substantially below assigned value and effects of such discount. Quantify each risk/effect to the extent practicable. State whether any risks differ for investors in any partnership and identify such partnerships and describe differences. Instruction: quantification should include, e.g., the amount of cost savings from combined administration compared to transaction costs, and if material conflicts arise from payments to sponsor/general partner, quantify such payments and compare to amounts they would be entitled to without the roll-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 905 — Comparative information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide comparative descriptions and analyses of rights, duties, compensation, distributions, policies and material terms between the successor and each partnership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (a)(1) describe voting and other rights of investors in the successor under governing instruments and law, compare to rights in each partnership and describe effects of changes; (a)(2) describe duties owed by successor's general partner and compare to duties owed by each partnership's general partner and describe effects; (b)(1)-(2) describe each item of compensation and each instance of cash/other distributions payable by the successor to the general partner and affiliates, comparing to current compensation/distributions and describe effects; (b)(3) provide a table demonstrating changes in compensation and distributions setting forth combined actual amounts paid by partnerships for last three fiscal years and interim periods and amounts that would have been paid if post-roll-up structure had been in effect; (b)(4) if proposed changes would materially change compensation/distributions, describe such changes and effects; (b)(5) describe material conflicts that may arise from compensation/distribution arrangements and steps to resolve; (c) describe governing instrument provisions and policies relating to distributions and compare to partnerships; (d) (1) describe each material investment policy of the successor and compare to partnerships (including borrowings); (d)(2) describe any plans of GP/sponsor/affiliate regarding sale/purchase/borrowings; (d)(3) state whether specific assets have been identified for sale/financing/purchase and describe if so; (e) describe other similar material terms or policies and compare and describe effects. Instructions: illustrate information in tables or other readily understandable formats and set information in appropriate separate sections of the principal disclosure document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 906 — Allocation of roll-up consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the method used to allocate interests in the successor to investors in the partnerships and provide supporting valuation calculations and tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe in reasonable detail the allocation method and reasons. Provide a table showing calculation of valuation of each partnership and allocation of interests in the successor, including for each partnership: (1) value assigned to each significant category of assets and total value assigned to the partnership; (2) total value assigned to all partnerships; (3) aggregate amount of interests in the successor to be allocated to each partnership and percentage of total; (4) amount of interests of the successor to be issued to investors per interest held in each partnership (on an equivalent interest basis, e.g., per $1,000 invested). If interests will be allocated to the general partner or it will receive other consideration, describe method used to allocate interests or determine consideration and reasons, and identify consideration paid by the general partner for interests to be exchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 907 — Background of the roll-up transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Furnish a summary of the background of the transaction, including contacts, negotiations and transactions, and describe background of each partnership and material financial developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a summary of contacts/negotiations/transactions concerning mergers, acquisitions, tender offers, changes in control, covering the period beginning with each partnership's second full fiscal year preceding the filing; include contacts between GP/affiliates and any person with a direct interest and identify who initiated such contacts. Briefly describe background of each partnership including amount of capital raised, extent net proceeds invested, extent funds invested as planned and amount not yet invested; partnership investment objectives and extent achieved. Discuss whether GP (including any affiliated person materially dependent on GP compensation) or any partnership has experienced or is likely to experience any material adverse financial developments since commencement of the most recently completed fiscal year and describe such developments and effects on the transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 908 — Reasons for and alternatives to the roll-up transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the reasons for the roll-up transaction and any alternatives considered, including continuation or liquidation alternatives, and the reasons for the transaction structure and timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the reason(s) for the roll-up. If alternatives were considered, describe the alternatives and reasons for rejection. Whether or not alternatives were considered, describe in reasonable detail the potential alternative of continuation of the partnerships in accordance with existing business plans (effects, material risks and benefits, and GP's reasons for not considering if applicable) and the potential alternative of liquidation (procedures, effects, material risks/benefits and GP's reasons for not considering if applicable). State reasons for the structure and timing of the roll-up. State whether GP initiated the roll-up and if not, whether GP participated in structuring. State whether GP recommends the roll-up and briefly describe reasons for recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 909 — Conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the general partner's fiduciary duties and each actual or potential material conflict of interest relating to the roll-up, and disclose whether an unaffiliated representative was retained for investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly describe GP's fiduciary duties to each partnership and each actual/potential material conflict of interest between GP and investors relating to the roll-up. State whether GP has retained an unaffiliated representative to act for investors; if not, describe reasons and risks from absence of separate representation. If retained, identify the representative; briefly describe qualifications including any similar transactions in past five years; describe method of selection including whether any investors were consulted and names if so; describe scope and terms of engagement including fee responsibility and whether fees are contingent; describe any material relationship between the representative (or affiliates) and GP, sponsor, successor or any other person with material interest in the roll-up that existed during past two years or is contemplated and any compensation received or to be received; describe in reasonable detail actions taken by the representative on behalf of investors; describe fiduciary duties or other legal obligations of the representative to investors in each partnership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 910 — Fairness of the transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the general partner reasonably believes the roll-up transaction is fair or unfair to investors and provide a detailed discussion of the material factors supporting that belief, with comparisons to alternatives and attention to differences among partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether GP reasonably believes roll-up is fair or unfair to investors and reasons, addressing fairness to investors in each partnership and as a whole and to each possible combination of partnerships or portions if applicable. Discuss material factors upon which belief is based and weight assigned to each factor, including analysis of factors set forth in related instructions and Items (e.g., Item 909(b)(1) and Item 911). The discussion must: (1) compare consideration to be received to consideration under each alternatives discussed in Item 908(b); and (2) describe any material differences among partnerships relating to fairness. If any offers were received and rejected, describe and state reasons for rejection. Describe any factors known that may materially affect values assigned or fairness conclusions. State whether GP's statements are based in whole or in part on any report/opinion/appraisal and, if so, describe material uncertainties related to such reports. Instructions enumerate factors normally important to determining fairness and weight (current/historic market prices, net book value, going concern value, liquidation value, purchases of limited partnership interests by GP/sponsor/affiliates, any report/opinion/appraisal, recent offers within 18 months). Conclusory statements are insufficient; consideration should be given to presenting comparative numerical data in tabular format and using most recent available financial information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 911 — Reports, opinions and appraisals
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose all material reports, opinions or appraisals from outside parties materially related to the roll-up transaction, with identification, qualifications, summaries, relationships, and exhibit filings; and provide special disclosure rules for fairness opinions and appraisals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether GP or sponsor has received any materially related report/opinion/appraisal from an outside party (other than counsel). For each such report identify the outside party; briefly describe its qualifications; describe method of selection; describe any material relationship between the outside party (or affiliates) and GP, sponsor, successor or affiliates existing during past two years or contemplated and any compensation received or to be received; state whether outside party recommended amount of consideration or GP determined it; furnish a summary of the report including procedures followed, findings/recommendations, bases and methods, instructions received from GP/sponsor/affiliates, and any limitation imposed on scope (and reasons); state whether compensation to outside party is contingent on approval/completion and reasons if so. Furnish a statement that upon written request an investor may receive a copy of any such report promptly without charge and provide contact. All such reports/opinions/appraisals shall be filed as exhibits to the registration statement. Describe contacts in connection with preparation of opinions (identity of parties, nature of contact, actions taken, views expressed, reasons party did not provide report). Fairness opinions: state whether opinion addresses fairness to investors in each partnership and all possible combinations; if not, identify combinations addressed, who determined which combinations and reasons, and state if roll-up is completed with a combination not addressed no opinion will have been obtained. If no opinion obtained, state reasons why not necessary. Appraisals: describe purpose(s) for which appraisals obtained and their use; describe which assets covered and aggregate appraised value (net of indebtedness) and any material qualifications and summary of qualifications; identify appraisal date and whether updates will be made and whether events since date may have caused material change; include appendix tables setting forth appraised value of any separately appraised significant asset, value under each valuation approach considered identifying approach and reasons chosen, and all material assumptions used by appraiser and reasons for different assumptions if used. Define 'significant' asset as one representing >10% of partnership value or producing >=10% of cash flow or net income for the period. Instructions note that reports/opinions/appraisals to be identified include those materially related whether or not relied upon (e.g., regarding alternatives) and information in (a)(2) should be given with respect to the firm providing the report rather than individual employees. A clear and concise summary of appraisals is required; do not include an appraiser's summary in lieu of required description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 912 — Source and amount of funds and transactional expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: State the source and total amount of funds or other consideration to be used in the roll-up transaction and provide an itemized statement of expenses and financing arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the source and total amount of funds or consideration to be used. Furnish a reasonably itemized statement of all expenses incurred or estimated in connection with the roll-up (filing fees, legal, financial advisory, accounting, appraisal fees, solicitation expenses, printing), and identify persons responsible for paying such expenses. State whether any partnership will be responsible (directly or indirectly) for any expenses, and if so, state the amount from each partnership and sources of capital to finance such amount. If any part of the consideration to be used by sponsor or successor is expected to be provided by any partnership, state amount to be provided by each partnership and sources of capital. If funds are expected to be borrowed by sponsor or successor for the roll-up, provide a summary of each loan agreement (identity of parties, term, collateral, stated and effective interest rates, and other material terms) and briefly describe plans or arrangements to finance or repay such borrowing or state if none. If source is an ordinary-course bank loan and section 13(d) or 14(d) applies, bank name may be withheld from public if filer files a written request naming such bank with the SEC Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 913 — Other provisions of the transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe appraisal rights, access to books and records, counsel/appraisal services provisions, and investors' rights to partnership lists under federal and state law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether appraisal rights are provided under applicable state law, under the partnership's governing instruments, or will be voluntarily accorded by the successor/GP/sponsor (or affiliates) and summarize such appraisal rights. If appraisal rights will not be available to investors who object, briefly outline rights which may be available to such investors under applicable law. If any provision allows investors access to books and records or to obtain counsel or appraisal services at the expense of the successor/GP/partnership/sponsor (or affiliates), describe such provision. Discuss investors' rights under federal and state law to obtain a partnership's list of investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 914 — Pro forma financial statements: selected financial data
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specified selected financial data and pro forma financial information for each partnership proposed to be included in the roll-up transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to information required by Item 302, for each partnership provide cash and cash equivalents, total assets at book value, total assets at the value assigned for roll-up (if applicable), total liabilities, general and limited partners' equity, net increase (decrease) in cash and cash equivalents, net cash provided by operating activities, distributions; and per unit data for net income (loss), book value, value assigned for roll-up (if applicable), and distributions (separately identifying distributions that represent a return of capital). Provide this information for the previous two fiscal years; include additional/other information if material to understanding each partnership. Provide pro forma financial information (including oil and gas reserves and cash flow disclosure if appropriate) assuming: (1) all partnerships participate in the roll-up; and (2) participation of those partnerships that on a combined basis have the lowest combined net cash provided by operating activities for the last fiscal year of such partnerships, provided participation by such partnerships satisfies all conditions to consummation of the roll-up transaction.
